##  Seismic hazard

<ID.51188AC5> site.  A *Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment* (PSHA) rigorously quantifies the input from all seismic sources considering the full range of possible earthquake magnitudes that could affect the area. In this chapter, the most relevant findings for the definition of seismic design parameters are summarized.


In a probabilistic framework, the ground motion intensity is expressed in terms of its *annual exceedance probability* (AEP). The AEP is the rate of exceedence of a specific level of seismic intensity due to the potential occurrence of earthquakes from that source over a one-year period. The Return Period <ID.6BB27EFA> is defined as the inverse of the AEP. The methodology employed for estimating the AEP is based on the Cornell-McGuire methodology, as referenced by @Cornell1968, and @McG04, which combines earthquake occurrence models, seismic source zone models, magnitude-recurrence relationships, and ground-motion intensity models through the total probability theorem. The *spectral ordinate* <ID.BD09C494> is the maximum acceleration reported by a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) oscillator with fundamental period <ID.8DC523A7> and represents the seismic ground-motion defined of a given target service level for each structural period. 

<ID.D854B4E2>


The *response spectra* represent spectral ordinates <ID.BD09C494> expressed in terms of the SDOF's fundamental period <ID.8DC523A7> for a given target annual exceedance probability (AEP). The *uniform hazard spectra (UHS)* represents spectral ordinates <ID.BD09C494> with the same probability of exceedance defined for all structural periods <ID.8DC523A7>. 

<ID.6A2D912C>

*Design Ground Motions* for critical infrastructure will have a target Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) defined according to the failure consequences rating for a given target service level (construction, operation, closure, or post-closure). The consequence-based seismic design of a critical facility must ensure a very low probability of failure for extreme events and an acceptable level of damage for earthquakes likely to occur during the service life of the facility.

> The design of the tailings storage facilities in <ID.1C838F53>, is based on a service level of 5,000 years for the operational earthquake (OBE) and 10,000 years for the maximum design earthquake (MDE) during the closure and post-closure phases.
